messages:
maria: heads up — eu1-gpu pool: ~12 pods in model-serving are stuck Terminating after we tried to roll a canary. kubelet logs show AttachVolume/DetachVolume timeouts and the nvidia device-plugin isn't releasing resources. :grimacing:
ashish: yikes. saw similar in us-west last month. is this the attach/detach API to the cloud provider hanging or something at the kernel/CNI level?
k8s-alert-bot: [ALERT] PersistentVolumeDetachErrors on nodes gpu-eu1-*-pool (12 occurrences in last 6m)
maria: quick paste from kubelet log on gpu-eu1-12:
```
I0308 02:14:07.123456  1234 attach_detach_controller.go:432] error detaching volume "pvc-6f3a" from node gpu-eu1-12: rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded desc = context deadline exceeded
E0308 02:14:07.123789  1234 device_plugin.go:211] nvidia device plugin: failed to release device for pod model-serving/api-123: timeout waiting for RPC
```
kyra: are we seeing any network egress shaping on those hosts? last week network team enabled tc-based shaping on bursty tenants in eu1 to cap noisy neighbors.
ben: checking monitoring — host-level egress out of gpu-eu1 AZ shows a 400–700Mbps sustained burst cap by our CNI policer between 02:00–03:00. iperf between nodes shows spikes then stalls.
maria: that would explain attach/detach RPCs timing out (they're tunneled over host network to cloud block storage control plane). If the detach can't complete the kubelet leaves the pod in Terminating while the device-plugin still holds the GPU.
nashish: short term mitigation: can we (1) disable graceful termination for model-serving canaries, or (2) increase AttachDetachReconcileSyncPeriod so controller retries longer? Also maybe bump CNI policer for gpu nodes.
kyra: ops-oncall — can you temporarily lift the egress cap for the gpu-eu1 pool and watch the attach/detach errors?
ops-oncall: I can do a scoped lift for 30m on the pool. Rolling it now. Will post when done.
ben: after lifting cap i see attach RPC RTTs drop from 4.2s -> 180ms and device-plugin freed 8 GPUs within 2m. Pods finished terminating. :thumbsup:
maria: nice. postmortem notes — root cause appears to be aggressive host-level egress shaping colliding with cloud control plane RPC patterns (detach/attach + plugin healthchecks). That left GPUs stranded and blocked new allocations, causing scheduling pressure and forced backfilling on other AZs.
nashish: long-term fixes to consider:
- change device-plugin to use local unix domain socket fallback for detach confirmation where supported
- adjust CNI policer rules: exempt attach/detach RPC ports or add burst windows for control-plane ops
- add a descheduler job that evicts low-priority GPU pods stuck in Terminating after N minutes (with safe fallback)
- add a preemptive spare capacity policy for each AZ (1–2 nodes) to avoid cross-AZ spill when minor network blips occur
kyra: also add a metric/alert for "gpu-held-by-terminating" count so we catch this earlier.
maria: agreed. I'll open a short RFC for the policer exemption + alerting and a runbook for the oncall steps (lift cap, watch attach RTTs, reschedule). Will also add a note to the Dedicated provisioning playbook to reserve 1 spare GPU node per AZ.
ops-oncall: FYI the scoped lift is ending in ~5m. so far steady.
ben: can we avoid disabling policers widely? maybe instead mark control-plane port ranges as high-priority in tc filter. That seems safer.
nashish: SGTM. I'll pair with networking to validate ports and do a canary change in eu1 tomorrow morning low-traffic window.
maria: thanks all. updating incident channel with summary and linking this thread. :eyes:
